title: TypeScript paginated list client
context: Client for a REST list endpoint. Pages are 0-based (page=0 is the first page) and the server returns {items, total}. Filter values are free text typed by users. listAll must return every item, fetch at most maxPages pages, and fail (reject) if any page request fails.
code: export function buildUrl(base: string, q: ListQuery): string {
export async function fetchPage<T>(base: string, q: ListQuery, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<PageResult<T>> {
const r = await fetch(buildUrl(base, q), { signal, headers: { Accept: "application/json" } });
if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`list failed: HTTP ${r.status}`);
export async function listAll<T>(base: string, filters: Record<string, string>, pageSize = 100, maxPages = 50): Promise<T[]> {
res = await fetchPage<T>(base, { page, pageSize, filters });

expected.why: filter values are not URL-encoded, so text containing & or = injects extra parameters or breaks the query
pages are 0-based, so starting at 1 skips the first page (and fetches only maxPages - 1 pages)
a failed page is swallowed and listAll resolves with a silently truncated list instead of rejecting
